quote: Okay. Thanks. So you're a little bit newer to the area. It's exciting.
stewart_read: Rep uses the residence-length answer to build light rapport rather than just logging it, a small positive move in an otherwise mechanical verify sequence.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as a model of turning a verify checkbox into a natural conversational beat — worth noting as a strength to keep.

quote: K. And then I have you down as the property owner. Is there anybody else on the title of the home with you?
stewart_read: Rep correctly runs the co-owner check per protocol; customer confirms no one else is on title (00:00 marker '01:21 rep: No.'), so no spouse-inclusion protocol is triggered — this is a clean, complete verify item with no follow-up action needed.
coaching_implication: No coaching action needed here — flag as a completed checklist item, useful for confirming the rep didn't skip this required verify step.

stewart_read: Customer discloses a high monthly bill in the same flat register used throughout the call — this is a strong anchor number, not an emotional cue, and the rep's job was to capture and flip it regardless of delivery tone.
coaching_implication: Use this number in the 1-on-1 to show the rep had the raw material for a flip and treated it as a data point instead.

quote: But we can definitely help you get that cut down quite a bit.
stewart_read: Rep acknowledges the $600 bill is expensive and offers generic reassurance, but never flips it into 'that $600 is the reason to act' — the ask-acknowledge-move-on pattern per coaching_philosophy.bill_anchoring failure_pattern.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be deliberately holding the emotional flip for the closer to deliver with the actual proposal numbers.
coaching_implication: This is a setter-level move, not closer-tier content — coach the rep to tie the bill number directly into urgency ('that $600 a month is exactly what this program is built to eliminate') before moving to qualifiers.

quote: I'm not looking for that right now.
stewart_read: Customer declines to pull up the bill live; this is general timing resistance, not a technical/navigation barrier — she never indicates she can't find the graph, only that she won't right now. The rep had no curiosity hook built earlier (no bill flip) to draw her back in at this moment of friction.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep's two-touch persistence before pivoting to text could reflect competent adaptive handling rather than failure.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep that an earlier bill-flip moment would have given them leverage to reference here ('I know that $600 bill is the whole reason we're doing this — let's get it locked in now') instead of a flat re-ask.

quote: What I could do is I could send you a text, and then just whenever you have a minute, if you could just screenshot that and send it over to me.
stewart_read: The call ends with a bill-collection workaround but no appointment is ever proposed, no day/time offered, and no button-up handshake occurs — the call simply stops after the text promise.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be following organic-lead flow where bill isn't required before booking, but no appointment offer appears anywhere in the transcript regardless of lead type.
coaching_implication: Flag that this call never reached appointment_set at all — the rep should have offered a specific day/time for the closer call before or alongside the text-follow-up ask, rather than ending on 'we will keep in touch.'
